architecture.name: flashinfer-sm75-gap
architecture.head_dims: FA2 prefill/decode template family supports head_dim 64/128/256; on sm_75 the validated working subset is FP16 d=64/128/256. head_dim 512 (Gemma-4) is SM120/121-only (PR #3576); MLA dims (576/512) are SM80+ only. The June-2026 regressions #3528 and #3620 were at d=256 and d=128 respectively.
architecture.qkv_dim_divergence: Asymmetric head_dim_qk != head_dim_vo exists in the codebase (e.g. NVFP4 qk=512/vo=256 asymmetric VO-split paged prefill for Gemma-4, PR #3684, merged 2026-08-13) but that path explicitly targets SM120/121; the sm_75-verified evidence (RTX 2080 Ti test runs on PR #3526, T4 runs on PR #3621) is all symmetric qk=vo. [uncertain] whether any asymmetric qk/vo combination is valid within sm_75's 64 KiB smem cap - the FP8-KV asymmetric attempt on 2080 Ti failed dispatch (NUM_MMA_D_QK=16 NUM_MMA_D_VO=16 invalid configuration, #3621 comments, July 2026).
architecture.kv_heads_gqa: GQA/MQA is handled by the paged-KV wrapper layer (BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper / BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheWrapper, NHD and HND page layouts) and is architecture-independent; no sm_75-specific KV-head constraint was found in any issue. The #3620 T4 repro served a GQA model (Nemotron-Nano-9B) through vLLM's wrapper path.
architecture.hybrid_pattern: On sm_75 FlashInfer only offers the standard full-attention FA2 kernels plus decode/sampling. The newer linear-attention / Gated DeltaNet ('cake_gdn', 'cake_kda', 'cake_mamba') backends are SM100/SM103+ only (PRs #4581, #4279, #4616, Aug 2026); MLA is SM80+. [uncertain] No explicit statement that hybrid models are blocked on sm_75, inferred from arch annotations in release notes and zread architecture docs.
architecture.heterogeneous_dims: Per-layer head-dim divergence (Gemma-4 qk=512/vo=256 globals) is handled only by the SM120/121 NVFP4 asymmetric VO-split kernel. Nothing on sm_75 supports heterogeneous dims; models with such shapes cannot use FlashInfer prefill on Turing.

kernel_support.supported_dims: Achieved via C++ template instantiation + on-device JIT keyed per arch (cache path e.g. '~/.cache/flashinfer/0.6.12/75/generated/batch_prefill_...head_dim_qk_128_head_dim_vo_128_...', seen in #3620 - JIT compilation for sm_75 works, the failures are launch-config, not compile). Prefill dispatch clamps NUM_MMA_KV against a runtime shared-memory budget: max_smem_per_threadblock = min(cudaDevAttrMaxSharedMemoryPerMultiprocessor/num_ctas_per_sm, cudaDevAttrMaxSharedMemoryPerBlockOptin); on sm_75 the opt-in cap is 65536 B. head_dim 256 FP16 fits with NUM_MMA_KV=1 only after PR #3526 (merged 2026-07-22) removed 48 B of alignas(16) placeholder padding from SharedStorageQKVO: sizeof went 65584 -> 65536 (FP16), 65568 -> 65536 (FP8), 50192 -> 50176 (NVFP4). Decode kernels use small per-page KV tiles and have no documented 64 KiB problem at d<=256. Sampling kernels fixed for 2080 Ti in Sept 2025 (#1697 'too many resources requested for launch' -> PR #1727).
kernel_support.capability_gate: Nominal floor: JIT check_cuda_arch() accepts sm>=7.5 (flashinfer/jit/core.py on main: 'FlashInfer requires GPUs with sm75 or higher' raised only if ALL detected archs < 7.5); README GPU Support table lists Turing SM 7.5 (T4, RTX 20 series) and 'Support for SM75 (Turing) and later (through Blackwell)'; the jit-cache wheel arch list includes 7.5 ('7.5 8.0 8.9 9.0a 10.0a 10.3a 10.7a 11.0a 12.0f'). REAL blockers: (1) Turing's 64 KiB per-block opt-in smem (vs 99 KB SM86/89/120/121, 164 KB SM80+) gives zero headroom, so host-side smem under-estimates become launch failures (cudaFuncSetAttribute -> cudaErrorInvalidValue 'invalid argument'); (2) no sm_75 attention CI, so regressions ship: maintainer yzh119 in #1648 (2025-09-07): 'We have a subset of kernels that are compatible with SM75, the only issue is test coverage (we don't have a SM75 CI machine...)'; same admission in #421 (2024-08-05: 'I don't have a sm_75 dev machine at the moment'); (3) FP8/FP4 paths not native to sm_75 (FP8-KV prefill dispatch fails on 2080 Ti); (4) historically inaccurate prefill configs fixed in v0.1.6 era (#448 accuracy 2024-08-15, #449 kernel configuration 2024-08-27, #472/#473 bf16 hotfixes, #473 'skip prefill kernels on sm75 for bf16'). History shows the support rot-clock: worked v0.1.6 (Aug 2024) -> drifted unsupported through 2024-2025 (#421, #1648, README dropped to 'SM80+') -> README/jit-cache re-include SM75 by 2026 -> two launch-failure regressions June 2026 (#3528 d256, #3620 batch paged prefill).
kernel_support.fallback_semantics: Three distinct failure modes. (1) Kernel level: dispatched sizeof(SharedStorage) > 65536 B fails at cudaFuncSetAttribute(cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize) with cudaErrorInvalidValue, surfaced as 'BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCache failed with error invalid argument' (#3620) - a hard launch failure at first use, no fallback, after plan() already succeeded (so the wrapper layer cannot preempt it). Current main adds a clearer FLASHINFER_ERROR: 'Even the smallest KV tile for head_dim_qk=..., head_dim_vo=... exceeds this GPU's N bytes of shared memory per block; this configuration is not supported on this architecture.' (2) Dispatch level: 'FlashInfer Internal Error: Invalid configuration : NUM_MMA_Q=1 NUM_MMA_D_QK=16 ...' for FP8-KV prefill on 2080 Ti (#3621 comments). (3) JIT gate level: check_cuda_arch() can FALSE-POSITIVE on supported GPUs when the torch build's TARGET_CUDA_ARCHS omits the running device - originally based on torch's _get_cuda_arch_flags raising 'FlashInfer requires sm75+' wrongly (#1101, fixed by PR #1598 2025-08-28), still misfiring on a 5090 under CUDA 12.8 (#3675, open) and on SM 12.0 via string comparison (#3945, fixed July 2026); HF gpt-oss-120b discussion #48 documents users on T4 hitting 'FlashInfer requires sm75+' and working around by disabling FlashInfer or rebuilding from source. At the vLLM layer there IS a clean fallback: vLLM's supports_compute_capability() floor of SM80 keeps FlashInfer from being auto-selected on SM75, so users silently get another attention backend.
kernel_support.ci_hardware_coverage: GitHub-hosted workflows have no GPU runners; real CI runs on NVIDIA-internal Jenkins/GitLab (nv/flashinfer-ci) via the /bot command. Since PR #1705 (merged 2025-09-21, still present in main Jenkinsfile) there is ONE sm_75 stage: 'JIT-Unittest-G4-cu129' on AWS G4 (T4) spot instances, with the comment 'For now, we only enable sampling test for SM75' - i.e. sampling kernels only, NO attention (prefill/decode) sm_75 CI. Consequence, demonstrated: the June 2026 NVFP4/FP8 staging-placeholder change (#3097/#3485) added 48 B to SharedStorageQKVO and silently broke all d=256 prefill on SM75/SM70 for ~6 weeks until a user (mikekg) reported #3528 and fixed it in #3526, whose PR text states 'the 64 KiB opt-in shared-memory cap is not exercised by upstream CI (SM80+)'. PR #3621's internal pipeline failed (1/20 passed) and the maintainer asked for conflict resolution instead of testing. Community sm_75 verification (RTX 2080 Ti / T4 runs attached to #3526 and #3621) is currently the only real attention coverage for Turing.

performance.turing_baseline: No published FlashInfer latency/throughput numbers on Turing exist; all sm_75 evidence is correctness/launch data. Verified-on-hardware data points: (a) PR #3526 author ran the d=256 test matrix on RTX 2080 Ti after the fix - test_single_prefill.py -k 256: 60 passed; test_batch_prefill_kernels.py -k 256 (FP16, paged/ragged): 868 passed; all of these fail to launch (cudaErrorInvalidValue) without the fix. (b) PR #3621 author ran vLLM end-to-end on Tesla T4 serving nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2-NVFP4 with CUDA-graph capture and correct output; a 2x 2080 Ti user (DiegoSVilla) confirmed paged prefill 'worked perfectly without kv quant' (vLLM 0.23). (c) 2024 baseline (esmeetu, #421): a vLLM fork mixing xformers prefill + FlashInfer decode on sm_75 (github.com/esmeetu/vllm/tree/sm75-flashinfer) performed 'almost same' as pure xformers - i.e., no FlashInfer prefill speedup was ever demonstrated on Turing; maintainer yzh119 explicitly does not expect Turing perf wins ('small shared memory size and missing of async copy features' vs Ampere, #421 thread 2024-08-08). [uncertain] No quantitative T4/2080Ti benchmark of FlashInfer attention was found.
performance.d256_feasibility: Yes for FP16/NVFP4 prefill, with ZERO headroom: the q/k/v union of SharedStorageQKVO alone fills the entire 65536 B opt-in budget on SM75/SM70 at head_dim 256 (pre-#3526 numbers: FP16 sizeof=65584 B, FP8=65568 B - both over; NVFP4=50176 B - fits; #3526/#3528 tables). Therefore d=256 prefill on sm_75 runs only with NUM_MMA_KV=1 and only if every auxiliary buffer (NVFP4 scale-factor planes k_sf_smem/v_sf_smem, FP8 kv_smem_repack, VO-split p_smem) is excluded via empty-base-struct (EBO) mixins or time-shared - which is exactly the mechanism PR #3526 landed (KVScaleFactorSmem / KVRepackSmem / VOSplitSmem empty bases + nullptr-returning accessors). Any future +1-byte struct growth re-breaks Turing (this fragility caused #3528). FP8-KV d=256 prefill cannot fit (65536 B + staging > 64 KiB). Decode at d=256 is comfortable (per-page KV tiles, split-KV); head_dim 512 prefill (Gemma-4) does not fit on sm_75 at all and is officially SM120/121-only.
performance.cost_analysis: For a d=256 sm_75 prefill kernel: q tile alone = CTA_TILE_Q x 256 x 2 B (32768 B at CTA_TILE_Q=64), leaving exactly 32768 B for one KV tile (NUM_MMA_KV=1, 16 rows x 256 x 2 B = 8192 B per K or V plane at NUM_WARPS_KV=4 sharing) plus warp-reduction scratch - no double-buffering or multi-tile pipelining possible; occupancy budget assumes 2 CTAs/SM only if max_smem_per_sm >= 2x the config (64 KiB/SM total on Turing makes 1 CTA/SM the norm, unlike the dispatch formula's Ampere+ assumption). Turing lacks cp.async, so K/V loads are synchronous (maintainer: performance expectations explicitly low, #421). Compile cost: sm_75 kernels arrive via on-device JIT (per-config nvcc invocation; wheelhouse/JIT-cache packages exist to avoid it - flashinfer-jit-cache arch list includes 7.5). Fix-implementation cost for upstream (per PR #3621, +79/-36 lines in one file): sample sizeof(SharedStorageQKVO<...>) at two tile counts to recover per-tile bytes + fixed base, clamp to cudaDevAttrMaxSharedMemoryPerBlockOptin, plus the SharedStoragePaged kEnableVOSplitOpt=true variant for HEAD_DIM_VO>=512.

design_fit.route: Primarily route C (bridge-header completeness for unmodified FA2/FlashInfer): the 2026 sm_75 breakages are host-side launch-accounting bugs (smem estimate vs actual struct size), not ISA limitations - T4/2080 Ti JIT-compile and run the kernels fine once sizeof is honored, so an unmodified-FlashInfer bridge only needs correct smem budgeting + a supported head-dim set. Secondarily informs routes A/B: d=256 on sm_75 has exactly 65536 B of smem available with NUM_MMA_KV=1, so both a native d=256 template (A) and k-chunked-256 (B) must budget against cudaDevAttrMaxSharedMemoryPerBlockOptin at runtime and cannot assume Ampere-style headroom.
design_fit.recommendation: For the sm_75 bridge kernel plan: (1) treat FlashInfer on Turing as 'decode + sampling usable, batch prefill gated' - do not build on FlashInfer prefill for production sm_75 until PR #3621 (or its already-landed main equivalents #3526 + #4767) is validated on real T4/2080 Ti hardware and vLLM reverts its floor (vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py supports_compute_capability() currently requires >= (8,0) with the comment 'revert to DeviceCapability(7, 5) once it [PR #3621] lands'; added in vLLM PR #45375, 2026-06-23, still present on main as of 2026-09-06). (2) Upstream un-gating requires exactly three things: a T4/G4 CI shard extended beyond sampling to the attention test matrix (the Jenkins GPU-G4 stage already exists - only the test scope needs widening), merge of the outstanding smem-accounting fix, and the one-line vLLM revert; AOT/jit-cache wheel coverage for 7.5 already exists. (3) For d=256 specifically: the working subset includes d=256 FP16 with NUM_MMA_KV=1 and no spare smem bytes - design the bridge kernel with EBO-style optional buffers and runtime sizeof sampling from day one, and avoid FP8-KV paths entirely on Turing.
design_fit.numerics_risks: Documented wrong-output history on sm_75: 2024 prefill produced incorrect results after manual tile-parameter tuning (esmeetu, #421: 'After tuning some parameters, it work but got wrong result') - the pre-#448/#449 era; resolved in v0.1.6. FP8-KV is not native to sm_75 and currently fails dispatch rather than degrading (#3621 comments, two 2080 Ti users, July 2026). Accumulation: DTypeQKAccum defaults to float for the FA2 family (half only if USE_FP16_QK_REDUCTION), so d=256 accumulation order is the standard split-KV float merge - but the 2026 sentinel/softmax bug cluster (#4267, #4450, #4451: zeros for rows with all logits below the -5e4 sentinel; #4401 extreme negative logits in masked softmax; #3890 LogitsTransform on lanes beyond split-KV chunk) shows the numerics edge cases that CI-covered arches catch; sm_75 has no attention CI, so equivalent Turing-specific numerics bugs would ship undetected. RoPE-llama smem path only triggers above HEAD_DIM_QK 256, so d=256 avoids that extra buffer.
design_fit.demand_weighting: High installed-base demand but low vendor priority. T4 is the canonical low-cost cloud/Colab GPU and the RTX 20-series a large consumer base - the #1648 appeal ('Tesla T4 and the RTX 20xx series are still the most common GPUs in the market', closed as not-planned Aug 2026) and the six community bumps on PR #3621 ('Very needed update for SM75 compatibility') quantify it. Demand is sharpening: vLLM PR #45375 (2026-06-23) explicitly enabled modelopt_mixed (NVFP4) quantization ON Turing, and NVIDIA's Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2-NVFP4 is being served on T4s - yet the same month its FlashInfer attention broke (#3620), and vLLM hedges by not auto-selecting the backend. Maintainer stance (yzh119, #1648): willing to fix reported sm_75 bugs, unwilling to guarantee coverage without a CI machine; no official sm_75 AOT wheels, only jit-cache arch inclusion.

community_artifacts.wheels_and_forks: (1) mikekg's T4 wheelhouse gist (https://gist.github.com/mikekg/8b634d4235efe5f614b7bda98eaad651, June 2026): Colab-T4 wheelhouse (fleetwide_nvfp4_t4_wheelhouse.tgz on HF, sha256-verified) containing vLLM built from the fleetwide-nvfp4 branch (vllm-0.1.dev17315+g5afe87873), causal_conv1d 1.6.1, mamba_ssm 2.3.1, cp312/CUDA 13.0/glibc 2.35, plus a Colab notebook and install script; FlashInfer 0.6.12 kernels are JIT-compiled for sm_75 at runtime inside it. (2) esmeetu/vllm branch sm75-flashinfer (Aug 2024, stale): vLLM fork using xformers prefill + FlashInfer decode on sm_75; performance ~= xformers. (3) No official FlashInfer sm_75 AOT wheels; official jit-cache wheels do include sm_75 in their arch list. (4) HF openai/gpt-oss-120b discussion #48 documents the practical workaround set on T4: disable FlashInfer / force another attention backend, or rebuild FlashInfer from source for cc 7.5.
